topics.title: Section A: Dharma and Dharmic Living

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of dharma and the different ways the word is understood.
Describe how dharma relates to the Vedic idea of rita.
Explain how dharma relates to the other purusharthas: artha, kama and moksha.
Explain the relationship of dharma to moral behaviour.

subtopics.title: Dharmic society and the four ages

outcomes.text: Explain how Sadharana Dharma and Sanatana Dharma shape society.
Discuss whether morality is universal, relative or a mixture.
Describe the ideal dharmic society in terms of Sadharana Dharma and personal dharma.
Explain the concept of adharma.
Describe the cycle of four ages (Mahayuga) and the features of Satya, Treta, Dvapara and Kali Yuga.
Explain varna dharma and ashrama dharma and how they vary for individuals.
Discuss whether modern society can or should follow the ideal of varnas and ashramas.
Explain varnashramadharma as a united strategy for living and for ethical life.
Describe the difficulties and controversies around varnashramadharma in the modern world.
Judge the place of varna and ashrama in modern society.
Tell varna from jati and explain how they differ.
Explain the difficulties and inequalities linked to the caste system.
Evaluate how accurate it is to equate caste with varna.
Explain the meaning of svadharma as individual dharma.
Describe the factors shaping svadharma: varna, ashrama, conscience and circumstance.
Explain how context and personal factors complicate ethical choices.
Describe conflicts between dharmic duties, using Rama and Arjuna as scriptural examples.
Describe ways Hindus consider svadharma: prayer, conscience, scripture and spiritual guidance.
Explain the relationship between personal and universal dharma and its effect on life choices.
Explain dharma as it relates to women and their traditional roles.
Describe the requirements traditionally linked with sthri dharma.
Discuss how traditional roles are upheld or challenged in Hindu society.
Evaluate how far Lakshmi, Durga, Sita and Draupadi fit traditional expectations.
Evaluate how Hindu women today interpret or challenge sthri dharma.
Explain samsara as the cycle of birth, death and rebirth.
Describe why people become trapped in samsara: ignorance, karma and attachment.
Explain why people seek release from samsara.
Compare different attitudes towards samsara and liberation.
Explain maya as illusion, especially the illusory nature of the apparent universe.
Contrast maya as Brahman's creative power with maya as a veil hiding one's true nature.
Explain why maya may be an obstacle or a help towards liberation.
Explain karma as actions and their consequences, and its different forms.
Explain karma, vikarma and akarma.
Explain sakama and nishkama karma, and nishkama karma as the path to moksha.
Explain sanchita, prarabdha and agami karma.
Explain the role of karma in samsara and in achieving liberation.
Explain why human rebirth matters most for liberation.
Discuss how far karma can be considered just.
Explain ways of understanding moksha: oneness with Brahman or being with deity without being identical.
Explain jivan mukti and videha mukti and the traits of a jivan mukta.
Explain how different paths to moksha fit different understandings of the divine and self.
Describe how different Hindu traditions view moksha.
Explain the cat and monkey analogies for religious paths.
Discuss different views on the role of personal effort in achieving moksha.
Describe the jnana, karma, bhakti and raja margas.
Explain what each marga means for different individuals.

topics.title: Section A: Origins and Development of Hinduism

outcomes.text: Name the four Vedas and their concerns: hymns, songs, ritual and magic or medicine.
Describe the oral transmission of the Rig Veda.
Explain the unusual and debated status of the Atharva Veda.
Describe the Samhitas, Aranyakas, Brahmanas and Upanishads.

subtopics.title: Status and importance of the Vedas

outcomes.text: Explain shruti and smriti and the Vedas' usual status as shruti.
Tell astika from nastika traditions.
Explain the importance of Vedic writings and how Vedic Hinduism relates to Hinduism today.
Explain the epics' usual status as smriti.
Describe the nature and significance of the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita.
Explain the relationship between the Bhagavad Gita and the Mahabharata.
Outline the main events and points of each text.
Describe the different ways Hindus use and understand the epics' stories.
Explain how the stories relate to theistic traditions and Hindu practice.
Explain the epics' importance for Hindus.
Suggest why the epics are more widely known than the Vedas.
Describe the nature and concerns of the Manusmriti.
Explain the Manusmriti as laws on Hindu living and the roles of social groups.
Explain the different views on its status and why it is contested.
Describe its impact on Hindu life and different ideas about how to use it.
Evaluate its relevance today and the reasons for controversy.

topics.title: Section B: The Nature of Ultimate Reality

outcomes.text: Explain different understandings of the divine: nirguna and saguna Brahman, sat-chit-ananda, neti-neti, murti, ishvara and Devi/Shakti.
Explain saguna Brahman as knowable through deities and what this means for relating to the divine.
Explain nirguna Brahman and what it means for relating to the divine.
Discuss the knowability or unknowability of the divine and its implications.
Compare views of atman and Brahman as identical, same but eternally distinct, or separate created being.
Describe understandings of the divine as masculine, feminine or neither.
Explain the unity of Hinduism and the diversity of its traditions.
Name the core theistic traditions: Vaisnavism, Shaivism, Shaktism and Smartism.
Describe the main beliefs, practices and geographical influence of each tradition.
Identify areas of divergence and commonality within and between traditions.
Explain the influence and religious significance of these traditions for Hindus.
Explain why different traditions exist and why a Hindu might follow one.
Evaluate how far they are distinct and separate forms of Hinduism.

topics.title: Section B: The Nature of Ultimate Reality

outcomes.text: Explain henotheism, monism, monotheism, pantheism and polytheism.
Relate different forms of Hinduism to these theistic descriptions.
Explain how theistic perspective relates to atman and moksha.
Explain how theistic perspective relates to murti puja and meditation.
Explain the significance of these perspectives in Hindu thought and practice.
Explain the meaning of Samkhya.
Explain how Samkhya relates to theism, and to Yoga including Patanjali's Ashtanga Yoga.
Describe the origins of Samkhya, the life of Kapila and the influence of his context.
Explain Purusha and Prakriti, the three gunas and the evolution of the world.
Explain belief in many purushas but no ishvara, and the means of kaivalya.
Compare Samkhya with Ashtanga Yoga, including the eight limbs, and consider Kapila's possible influence on the Buddha.
Explain the meaning of Advaita Vedanta.
Describe the origins of the tradition, Shankara's life and the influence of his context.
Explain the identity of jiva atman with Brahman and nirguna Brahman.
Explain the world as maya and jnana as the path to moksha.
Explain the usefulness but ultimate unreality of ishvara and puja, and the three levels of reality.
Explain the meaning of Vishistadvaita Vedanta.
Describe the origins of the tradition, Ramanuja's life and the influence of his context.
Explain why Ramanuja deliberately challenged Advaita.
Explain the three real components: ishvara, chit and achit, and their relation to Brahman.
Explain the relationship of jiva-jagat to Brahman and the importance of saguna Brahman.
Explain the reality of the material world, and bhakti and puja as the path to moksha.
Explain the meaning of Dvaita Vedanta.
Describe the origins of the tradition, Madhva's life and the influence of his context.
Explain the dualistic universe and the real distinction between Brahman and jiva atman.
Explain the identification of Brahman with Vishnu and the difference between atman and Vishnu.
Explain bhakti as the only path to moksha and the importance of puja and devotion to Vishnu.
Describe the five differences: self and ishvara, matter and ishvara, selves, matter and self, and types of matter.
Describe different understandings of the word religion.
Explain the difficulties of calling Hinduism a religion.
Discuss whether the different Hindu traditions form a single religion.
Explain the implications of Hinduism being a term imposed from outside.
Describe Hinduism as a lived tradition and cultural identity.
Explain how scholarship of religion shapes how Hinduism is understood.
Explain pluralistic religion and its relationship to Hinduism.
Describe diversity in Hindu identity, and diversity and tolerance in Hindu society.
Explain how diverse traditions interact with Hinduism and how Hindus respond to non-Hindu religions.
Discuss what is or is not astika Hinduism.
Explain the relationship between Hinduism and the Shramana traditions.
Explain why the Shramana traditions arose and rejected the Vedas.
Discuss the debate about Hinduism's influence on the Shramana traditions.
Compare Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism on karma, rebirth and liberation.
Name Hindus who shaped how non-Hindus see Hinduism: Vivekananda and Gandhi.
Explain the impact of Gandhi and Vivekananda on understanding Hinduism as a world religion.
Explain Ramakrishna's influence on Vivekananda and Vivekananda's framing of Hinduism as a world religion.
Describe Gandhi's interest in Jainism and Christianity as sources of wisdom and ethics.
Explain Gandhi's presentation of ahimsa and vegetarianism as universal Hindu values, and satyagraha as a route to social justice.
Describe their influence on contemporary Hinduism and how non-Hindus understand it.
Study Hinduism in one country outside India with a large Hindu community.
Explain how physical and social context affects the practice of Hinduism.
Describe the origins and development of this Hindu community.
Describe religious issues for migrants, including the ban on brahmins crossing the sea.
Describe key festivals and how they are celebrated, including differences in emphasis.
Describe the origins of ISKCON and the Sathya Sai International Organisation.
Describe ISKCON practices: bhakti, community life, sankirtana, the four regulative principles, preaching and Food for Life.
Describe Sathya Sai practices: seeing the divine within, five virtues, japam, dhyaanam, bhajan and seva.
Explain ISKCON teachings: moksha through bhakti yoga, Krishna as supreme, parampara, scripture and women's spiritual equality.
Explain Sathya Sai teachings: Sai Baba as avatar, oneness of God, unity of religions, equality, love and self development.
Explain proselytisation in relation to these movements.
Explain the reasons for their popularity.
Discuss how far these movements can be considered Hindu.
Explain their influence on non-Hindu perceptions of Hinduism and their significance for Hinduism today.
Explain a secular state and Gandhi's ideal of equal status for all religions.
Discuss whether secularism creates religious freedom and tolerance.
Describe the relationship between Hinduism and other religions in one country studied.
Explain the rise of Hindu fundamentalism and the Hindutva movement.
Explain how Hindutva has influenced Hinduism and perceptions of it, and its relationship with India.
Describe the practical applications of varna and jati.
Describe the concept of varna in sacred texts.
Explain ethical issues raised by the jati system as practised today.
Describe reformers: Ram Mohan Roy and the Brahmo Samaj, Dayananda and the Arya Samaj, Gandhi, and Ambedkar.
Explain the impact of reform movements on caste and the status of dalits.
Explain reform movements within dalit groups and their significance.

subtopics.title: The rights and status of women

outcomes.text: Describe traditional Hindu views on women's rights and status.
Discuss different arguments on sati, dowry and roles within marriage.
Relate Lakshmi, Durga, Kali, Parvati, Sita and Draupadi to contemporary feminism.
Compare contemporary views on women's rights with Hindu views.
Describe concerns about women's rights from traditional practices: sati, dowry and marriage roles.
Describe reactions to gender-based violence.
Explain the importance of educating women and girls.
Describe the work of social reform movements, female reformers and women's collectives.
Explain how reform movements have addressed concerns over women's rights.
